Implement the plan.

### Outcome

The plan is implemented in a way that aligns with the project's purpose and architecture. Provide a brief summary organized by plan task: what changed, any important departures from the plan and why, and any unfinished work.

### Guardrails

- Follow established code patterns and put shared behavior in one place. Fix the underlying cause rather than each symptom separately.
- Keep code focused on one responsibility and preserve stable interfaces where possible. Split mixed responsibilities into separate files. Keep files relatively small, under roughly 1,000 lines where possible.
- Prefer clear, straightforward code and abstractions that make the behavior easier to understand and maintain.

{{templates.purpose}}

{{templates.architecture}}

checklist.description: Task #1 - Define provider, policy, and attempt concepts in Model. Give each provider a stable configuration ID independent of its executable, allowing multiple configurations of the same CLI. Define executable and argument templates, context transport, credential references, and optional output, availability, cost, and continuation capabilities. Define provider-or-policy selections, ordered subscription candidates, explicitly configured paid fallback, shared budget references, and structured selection reasons. Separate provider identity from shared account/capacity and spending-pool identities. Define precedence as explicit invocation selection, node selection, then system default. An explicit provider remains pinned; fallback requires a policy.
verification: Validate duplicate IDs, missing references, incompatible capabilities, invalid templates, and invalid spending amounts.
Demonstrate two configurations using the same executable with different arguments and credential references.

checklist.description: Task #2 - Persist system configuration and migrate existing providers. After P1, add a versioned provider/policy document at the shared refine-state root, with application-owned validation and revision-checked writes. Nodes store only an optional selection; clearing it restores inheritance. Integrate configuration with bootstrap, synchronization, conflict reporting, and node configuration copying. Seed equivalent definitions for Claude, Codex, Gemini, Copilot, smoke-ai, and existing generic executables from the current discovery/invocation behavior. Migrate saved node agent_cli choices without changing effective selection or enabling paid fallback. Make migration idempotent and preserve original configuration evidence. Retire competing agent_cli authority through a documented compatibility path; unrelated settings updates must not materialize inherited provider choices as overrides.
verification: Test fresh installation, legacy configurations, interrupted/repeated migration, and two-node synchronization.
Verify existing custom paths and provider choices survive migration and clearing a node override follows later system-default changes.

checklist.description: Task #3 - Drive provider execution from definitions. After P1-P2, refactor src/infrastructure/agents/discovery and invocation so configuration selects executable, arguments, and capabilities instead of provider-name switches. Support supervised invocation and optional interactive/resume commands using argv arrays and documented placeholders for prompt, prompt file, working directory, and session ID. Extend the existing prompt transport for stdin, arguments, and file delivery while retaining effective-environment size checks, private prompt artifacts, explicit runtime roots, and worktree validation. Resolve credential references locally at launch from environment variables or private local files; support existing CLI-managed authentication. Keep values out of synchronized definitions, command metadata, diagnostics, and exported evidence. Retain existing output parsers as selectable adapters and offer plain output plus configurable structured extraction or a documented local adapter command for other CLIs. Normalize output into text, session, availability, and usage facts.
verification: Use fake executables to inspect exact argv, stdin, file payloads, working directory, and environment, including paths containing spaces.
Verify built-in launch compatibility and that a new provider needs configuration only.
Test missing credentials, redaction, malformed adapter output, and unsupported interactive/resume capabilities.

checklist.description: Task #4 - Implement shared selection and availability behavior. After P1-P3, extend src/application/agents/provider_selection into the common resolver and selection service. Evaluate subscription candidates in configured order before eligible paid fallback. Optional bounded probes and normalized execution results distinguish available, exhausted with retry time, unavailable, and unknown states. Scope cached observations to the node and configured account/capacity identity; an installed executable alone does not prove capacity. With no probe, allow a controlled subscription attempt and learn from its result. Use bounded retries and cooldowns to prevent repeated failed launches. Recheck subscriptions after cooldown and select a recovered subscription at the next attempt boundary without interrupting useful running work. Missing executables or credentials receive explicit diagnostics; ordinary task failures and failed Quality/Governance verdicts do not trigger provider shopping.
verification: Test precedence, subscription ordering, exhaustion, unknown availability, cooldown expiry, recovery, and no configured fallback.
Confirm ordinary work failures do not masquerade as capacity exhaustion.

checklist.description: Task #5 - Enforce shared paid-spending admission. Before enabling P4 paid launches, implement application-owned budget reservations and settlement using integer monetary units, explicit currency and accounting periods, and attempt IDs for idempotency. A budget pool covers all configured providers, policies, Goals, and nodes sharing that refine-state system. Reserve a conservative enforceable maximum before launch; settle confirmed usage afterward. Unknown usage retains the reservation. Generic post-run cost estimates alone cannot enforce a limit: paid configurations must supply an enforceable per-attempt cap or bounded charge contract, otherwise report why automatic paid fallback is unavailable. For fleet coordination, use an authoritative Git-backed budget ledger with compare-and-swap publication on a dedicated ref through existing Git infrastructure; local file locks or ordinary eventual state synchronization are insufficient. A reservation is spendable only after confirmed publication. Keep this monetary admission authority separate from workflow advancement. Handle contention, ambiguous publication, crashes, cancellation, period rollover, and budget edits conservatively; never reclaim a potentially running attempt’s allowance solely because a timeout elapsed. When shared reservation authority is unreachable, subscription work can continue but new paid spending waits.
verification: Race two nodes for the last available allowance and prove their admitted total cannot exceed the pool limit.
Test duplicate requests, lost acknowledgments, crashes before/after spawn, unknown cost, rollover with outstanding reservations, and disconnected nodes.
Verify all paid entry points, including explicit provider selection and repair attempts, use the same admission path.

checklist.description: Task #6 - Integrate selection and preserve work across attempts. After P3-P5, route workflow Event/Skill execution, managed and interactive sessions, chat, direct CLI invocation/resume, and delegated maintenance through the shared launch decision. Audit current direct agent_cli reads and HostAgentProviderService calls so alternate paths cannot bypass selection or spending. Keep each launch’s provider definition revision and policy decision pinned. Record a distinct attempt with provider ID, policy/source, reason, availability evidence, budget reservation, process receipt, usage, and outcome, linked to existing invocation history. On a switch, confirm the previous process tree has exited, retain the same admitted worktree and files, and assemble continuation context from the current request, completed artifacts, retained output, and unfinished work. Resume native sessions only for compatible provider configuration and credential/session scope; otherwise start a fresh session with that handoff. Preserve workflow authority checks before replacement and completion, and do not replay already accepted results. Capacity waiting should use recoverable scheduling rather than holding a worker or checkout lock in a sleep loop.
verification: Run a fake subscription provider that edits a file and then exhausts capacity; verify the fallback sees and preserves that work.
Test restart during a switch, cancellation, superseded Round, late completion, incompatible session IDs, and successful completion before recovery.
Verify attempts remain visible and switches do not advance workflow independently.

checklist.description: Task #7 - Expose configuration and decisions through existing surfaces. After the shared application services exist, extend the agent/config/node CLI groups and daemon API to list, inspect, validate, save, and remove provider definitions and policies, choose the system default, and set or clear node selection. Refuse deletion of referenced definitions with actionable diagnostics. Replace hard-coded browser provider options in settings_runtime.js with catalog-backed provider/policy choices and an explicit inheritance option. Provide system-level provider, policy, and budget editing, local credential-reference diagnostics, and an effective-selection preview. Show actual provider and reason for every attempt in Goal/Skill history and process views, including fallback, subscription recovery, and spending-related waits. Distinguish reserved, confirmed, and unknown spending.
verification: Exercise equivalent CLI/API/browser edits and stale-revision conflicts.
Verify inherited selections update correctly and attempt history retains the definition revision used.
Check that credentials never appear in configuration responses or synchronized exports.

checklist.description: Task #8 - Verify the complete behavior and document operation. Extend provider invocation, Event lifecycle, session/chat, CLI surface, and multi-instance synchronization suites. Update the Agents, Settings, and persistence intent documentation plus a provider configuration runbook with two configurations of one CLI, local credential setup, migration, policy inheritance, budget guarantees, and unsupported-capability diagnostics. Use the repository’s test harness: cargo test for unit coverage and cargo test -- --full for the complete required suite. Report unavailable prerequisites and exact failures separately from passing checks.

Prove concurrent spending admission and secret exclusion using fixtures without real credentials or paid requests.
Confirm existing built-in and generic provider workflows remain functional after migration.

Outcome
Users can add, edit, and select named AI provider configurations without changing Refine code. Make this a simple, polished part of Refine that is easy to understand and pleasant to use.

This Round replaces the earlier scope and P1-P8 completion requirements. Automatic provider switching is not required. Do not implement selection policies, subscription-first routing, capacity probing/cooldowns, automatic paid fallback, shared spending orchestration, cross-provider handoffs, or automatic subscription recovery for this Round. When the selected provider fails or reaches its limit, report that clearly through the existing failure behavior; the user chooses what to do next.

Behavior
- A provider configuration has a stable ID and editable name, executable/path, distinct argument elements with supported context templates, context delivery, and local credential references where needed. Support two configurations of the same CLI with different arguments. Keep credential values outside synchronized state and diagnostics.
- Store shared definitions and a system default. Each node may select an override or inherit the default; clearing its override restores inheritance. Explicit invocation selection takes precedence. Show the effective provider clearly.
- Use the configured provider consistently through existing launch paths. Preserve existing built-in/custom provider behavior and supported session capabilities. Report invalid configuration and unsupported capabilities clearly. Keep one authoritative catalog and use existing validation, persistence, and conflict handling.

UX and UI
Inspect neighboring Settings screens and shared components first. The provider list and editor must feel like a first-class part of the same product: matching typography, spacing, alignment, hierarchy, buttons, action placement, modal behavior, and responsive layout. Reuse established components and design tokens.
- Make the list easy to scan, with obvious add/edit actions and clear shared-default versus node-override controls.
- Use labeled controls, sensible defaults, concise help, and ordered argument rows that preserve each argument exactly, including spaces and templates. Ordinary setup must not require editing JSON. Put less common options in expandable sections.
- Provide useful inline validation and clear loading, save, cancel, and success feedback. Preserve drafts through refreshes, failed saves, and revision conflicts, with a clear conflict-resolution action. Respect project/node context changes.
- Support keyboard navigation, visible focus, associated labels, normal modal focus/Escape behavior, and narrow screens without overflow. Aim for an uncluttered, coherent finished experience, not just functioning controls.

Starting point
You may ignore the earlier implementation and start fresh from current main if that is simpler and produces a better result. Reuse previous work only where it helps this outcome; do not complete or carry forward unwanted automation merely because it already exists. Preserve prior Round records, failures, logs, and available Git/worktree evidence. Work in the workflow-owned workspace through Refine's supported lifecycle.

Verification
Verify actual browser flows: add/edit a provider, configure two variants of one CLI, change the system default, set/clear a node override, and recover from invalid input and stale revisions without losing edits. Inspect desktop and narrow-screen renders against neighboring Settings and retain screenshots. Use fake providers to verify exact arguments/context, effective selection, compatibility, and credential exclusion. Run the repository's required checks, including cargo test and cargo test -- --full, sequentially; investigate failures and report exact results honestly. Tests for explicitly removed automatic-switching behavior are no longer acceptance requirements; update affected tests and documentation to match this scope while retaining useful coverage.

Finish with a concise report of delivered behavior, browser/visual evidence, validation results, and any remaining gaps. Refine owns workflow transitions, integration, and review.
